title: Enabling Memory-Efficient On-Device Learning via Dataset Condensation
problem: Edge devices must learn from streaming, unlabeled, non-i.i.d. data seen only once, while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and managing limited buffer capacity. Current data selection strategies lead to high information loss.
motivation: Edge devices face strict memory constraints for rehearsal buffers; naive data selection discards most information, limiting continual learning effectiveness.
method: Proposes pseudo-labeling for unlabeled incoming data, dataset condensation tailored for on-device learning, and a feature discrimination objective to improve class purity. Data is condensed into informative synthetic samples rather than discarded.
key_novelty: Pseudo-labeling and fast dataset condensation technique specifically designed for on-device continual learning without requiring clean labels.
contributions: Pseudo-labeling technique for handling unlabeled on-device streaming data
Fast dataset condensation method optimized for on-device scenarios
Feature discrimination objective for improving label purity under noisy pseudo-labels
56.7% relative accuracy improvement on CORe50 with one sample/class buffer
baselines: Existing buffer management and rehearsal-based continual learning methods
limitations: Evaluation limited to CORe50 dataset; applicability to other data distributions and model architectures not demonstrated.
primary_theme: Memory-efficient on-device continual learning via dataset condensation
